patches.old: - Implied dielectric constant: κ ≈ 5–7 (consistent with a mixed lipid/protein composition)
patches.new: - Implied thickness of the dielectric: rearranging C/A = κε₀/d with κ ≈ 2–3 gives d = κε₀/(C/A) ≈ (2.5)(8.85 × 10⁻¹²)/(1 × 10⁻²) ≈ 2 nm — the hydrophobic core alone, not the full ≈7 nm bilayer, because only the core behaves as the insulating gap
patches.reason: The stated κ ≈ 5–7 is both inconsistent with the lesson's own κ ≈ 2–3 for the bilayer, given twice elsewhere, and does not follow from its own numbers: 1 µF/cm² across d = 7 nm implies κ = (C/A)d/ε₀ ≈ 8. The standard resolution, and the one biophysics texts use, is the reverse calculation: with the measured κ ≈ 2–3 of the acyl-chain core, 1 µF/cm² corresponds to a dielectric gap of about 2–3 nm, which is the hydrophobic core rather than the whole bilayer.

patches.old: This corresponds to roughly 1 ion per 10,000 phospholipid molecules—a tiny fraction of the total ion concentration, which is why the bulk concentrations of ions are not appreciably altered by the membrane potential.
patches.new: Dividing by the elementary charge gives (7 × 10⁻⁴ C/m²)/(1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) ≈ 4 × 10¹⁵ net charges per square metre. With each phospholipid occupying about 0.65 nm², a square metre of membrane holds roughly 3 × 10¹⁸ lipids counting both leaflets — so the separated charge amounts to about one net ion per thousand phospholipids. That is a tiny fraction of the ions present, which is why firing an action potential does not measurably change the bulk concentrations on either side.
patches.reason: The stated 1 in 10,000 is off by roughly a factor of ten and the lesson gives no way to check it. The arithmetic from the lesson's own 7 × 10⁻⁴ C/m² gives about one charge per thousand lipids; showing the two steps lets a student verify the estimate instead of memorising a number.

patches.old: In myelinated neurons, **Schwann cells** wrap the axon in multiple layers of lipid membrane (myelin), dramatically increasing the effective insulation and reducing capacitance per unit length.
patches.new: In myelinated neurons, glial cells wrap the axon in multiple layers of lipid membrane (myelin), dramatically increasing the effective insulation and reducing capacitance per unit length. In the peripheral nervous system this is done by **Schwann cells**, each myelinating a single segment of one axon; in the central nervous system it is done by **oligodendrocytes**, each of which myelinates segments of several different axons. The MCAT tests that distinction directly.
patches.reason: Naming only Schwann cells is wrong for the central nervous system, where oligodendrocytes myelinate axons — a distinction the exam asks about explicitly, including the one-cell-one-segment versus one-cell-many-axons difference.

sources.title: Nature Communications (2019) — the hydrophobic acyl chains, dielectric constant about 2–3, form the membrane's parallel-plate capacitor at roughly 0.1–1 µF/cm²
Heimburg, "Electrical properties of polar membranes" (arXiv) — the hydrophobic core as the non-conductive dielectric and the ≈1 nm Debye screening length at physiological ionic strength

visual.title: Where the charge goes, and what it does to the field
visual.alt: A solid conductor with excess charge on its outer surface, zero field and constant potential inside, and the field leaving perpendicular to the surface; a shell around a charge plus Q showing minus Q induced inside and plus Q outside, with grounding draining the outer charge; a comparison of conductors, whose carriers migrate, with insulators, whose charges only polarise; a plot of field against radius showing zero inside a conducting sphere but a linear rise inside a uniformly charged insulating sphere, identical outside; and the membrane capacitor with its low-dielectric hydrophobic core.
visual.caption: Every property in this lesson follows from one sentence: if a field remained inside a conductor, the free charges would still be moving, and it would not be equilibrium. Note that the conducting and insulating spheres are indistinguishable from outside.
